{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of North Carolina|Governor]] | before_election = [[Roy Cooper]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Josh Stein]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }}{{Elections in North Carolina sidebar}} The '''2024 North Carolina gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[governor of North Carolina]]. It was held concurrently with the [[2024 United States presidential election in North Carolina|2024 presidential election]] and [[2024 North Carolina elections|other elections]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state attorney general [[Josh Stein]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] lieutenant governor [[Mark Robinson (American politician)|Mark Robinson]]. He succeeded Democratic incumbent [[Roy Cooper]], who was term-limited. Primary elections took place on March 5, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=ncsl.org}} Stein won the Democratic nomination with 70% of the vote over former state Supreme Court Justice [[Michael R. Morgan]] and Robinson won the Republican nomination with 65% of the vote over state treasurer [[Dale Folwell]]. Initially a tight race, Robinson's history of controversial statements and revelations of comments he made on a pornographic website led to Stein gaining a significant polling advantage. Stein went on to win the election by 14.8 percentage points, the largest margin for a gubernatorial candidate in North Carolina since [[Jim Hunt]] in [[1980 North Carolina gubernatorial election|1980]], as well as winning counties that had not voted Democratic since [[2008 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2008]] ([[Franklin County, North Carolina|Franklin]] and [[Jackson County, North Carolina|Jackson]]), [[2004 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2004]] ([[Alamance County, North Carolina|Alamance]], [[Brunswick County, North Carolina|Brunswick]], and [[Transylvania County, North Carolina|Transylvania]]), and [[1980 North Carolina gubernatorial election|1980]] ([[Cabarrus County, North Carolina|Cabarrus]] and [[Henderson County, North Carolina|Henderson]]). Stein was also the only Democrat in 2024 to win a gubernatorial race in a state [[Donald Trump]] won in the [[2024 United States presidential election|concurrent presidential race]]. Robinson became the first Republican gubernatorial candidate since [[1976 North Carolina gubernatorial election|1976]] to not flip a county in the state. Stein received more than three million votes, the most of any candidate in the history of statewide elections in North Carolina. He is the first Jewish governor of the state.{{cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/us-elections/article-827760|title=Josh Stein defeats Mark Robinson to become North Carolina's first Jewish governor|publisher=The Jerusalem Post|accessdate=November 5, 2024}} Analysts have credited Stein's large margin of victory with [[Coattail effect|helping]] down-ballot Democrats in [[2024 North Carolina elections|concurrent elections]]. Stein received 354,121 more votes than Harris, while Robinson received 657,114 votes less than Trump.{{cite news|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2024/11/north-carolina-election-democrats-governor-legislature/680570/|title=Democrats Actually Had Quite a Good Night in North Carolina|publisher=The Atlantic|accessdate=November 17, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/north-carolina-election-democrats-governor-stein-1548a39fc2207f187785d3a65b217b89|title=North Carolina Democrats find electoral success further down the ballot and hope to build on it|publisher=Associated Press|accessdate=November 17, 2024}} According to exit polls, Stein won independent voters by 23 percentage points, which contributed to Robinson's defeat. Following his loss, Robinson retired from politics. == Background == A typical [[swing state]], North Carolina is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple to slightly red]] southern state at the federal level. Both [[United States Senate|U.S. senators]] from the state are members of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. Democrats and Republicans both hold multiple statewide offices in North Carolina. In the [[2020 United States presidential election in North Carolina|2020 presidential election]], [[Donald Trump]] carried North Carolina by 1.34 percentage points, the smallest margin among the states he won.{{Cite web |date=November 8, 2022 |title=Republican Ted Budd wins North Carolina's U.S. Senate race |url=https://apnews.com/article/north-carolina-senate-race-2022-midterm-elections-73fbfc2a6b07c87097b730bd44d42db9 |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=AP NEWS |language=en}} Incumbent [[Roy Cooper]] was first elected in [[2016 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2016]], defeating then-incumbent governor [[Pat McCrory]] by about 0.2 points. Cooper was re-elected in [[2020 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2020]] by 4.5 percentage points.{{cite web |title=State Composite Abstract Report - Contest.pdf |url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/State_Board_Meeting_Docs/2020-11-24/Canvass/State%20Composite%20Abstract%20Report%20-%20Contest.pdf |website=North Carolina State Board of Elections |access-date=November 24, 2020}}{{cite web |date=November 8, 2016 |title=North Carolina Official General Election Results |url=http://er.ncsbe.gov/?election_dt=11/08/2016&county_id=0&office=COS&contest=0 |access-date=January 5, 2017 |publisher=North Carolina State Board of Elections}} The [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee was [[Josh Stein]], the incumbent state attorney general. The [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee was [[Mark Robinson (American politician)|Mark Robinson]], the incumbent lieutenant governor.{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Elena |title=North Carolina AG Josh Stein launches bid for governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/01/18/north-carolina-ag-josh-stein-launches-bid-for-governor-00078281 |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=Politico |date=January 18, 2023 |language=en}} The 2024 election was initially expected to be competitive due to the state's nearly even to slightly right-leaning partisan lean, the concurrent presidential election, and the seat being open due to term limits. However, Robinson later became embroiled in numerous controversies after becoming the nominee, allowing Stein to open up a large and consistent lead in polls. Stein won 37 counties and Robinson won 63. Of the three gubernatorial races that went blue in 2024, North Carolina went bluest in its overall margin, even though the other two were significantly more Democratic states.{{cite news |last1=Cunningham |first1=Eric |title=Ratings Update: Mark Robinson Scandals Shift North Carolina Gubernatorial Race Shifts to Safe Democratic |url=https://elections-daily.com/2024/09/19/ratings-update-robinson-allegations-shift-north-carolina-gubernatorial-race-shifts-to-safe-democratic/ |access-date=September 19, 2024 |work=Elections Daily |date=September 19, 2024}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Josh Stein]], [[North Carolina Attorney General]] (2017–2025) ==== Eliminated in primary ==== * Chrelle Booker, [[Tryon, North Carolina|Tryon]] city councilor (2019–present) and candidate for U.S. Senate in [[2022 United States Senate election in North Carolina|2022]]{{cite news |work=[[Tryon Daily Bulletin]] |access-date=December 9, 2023 |url=https://www.tryondailybulletin.com/2023/12/07/tryon-councilwoman-eyes-north-carolina-governor-seat/ |date=December 7, 2023 |author=Langston, Grant |title=Tryon councilwoman eyes North Carolina governor seat}} * Gary Foxx, former [[Princeville, North Carolina|Princeville]] police chief{{cite web |last1=Mikkelsen |first1=Emily |last2=Melrose |first2=Justyn |title=Election 2024 North Carolina: These are the candidates who filed for races impacting the Piedmont Triad |url=https://myfox8.com/news/politics/your-local-election-hq/election-2024-north-carolina-these-are-the-candidates-who-filed-for-races-impacting-the-piedmont-triad/ |publisher=[[WGHP]] |access-date=December 18, 2023 |date=December 15, 2023}} * [[Michael R.
